record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: Characterize those Banach spaces X for which there exists an equivalent norm on X having numerical index 1; equivalently, characterize when 1 belongs to the renorming set N(X).

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Characterize those Banach spaces which can be equivalently renormed to have numerical index 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Banach space over the real or complex field, with norm ||·||, and let B_X, S_X, and X* denote its closed unit ball, unit sphere, and topological dual, respectively. For a bounded linear operator T: X → X, define its numerical radius by
   v(T) = sup{ |x*(T x)| : x ∈ S_X, x* ∈ S_{X*}, x*(x) = 1 }.
The numerical index of X is defined as
   n(X) = inf{ v(T) : T ∈ L(X), ||T|| = 1 } = max{ k ≥ 0 : k·||T|| ≤ v(T) for all T ∈ L(X) }.
For an isomorphic class, the renorming set is
   N(X) = { n(Y) : Y is a Banach space isomorphic to X },
i.e., the set of values of the numerical index attainable by equivalent renormings of X.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization, in terms of isomorphic (linear-topological) invariants of X, of those Banach spaces X for which 1 ∈ N(X), that is, those Banach spaces that admit an equivalent norm under which the numerical index equals 1.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing Banach spaces admitting an equivalent renorming with numerical index 1 is widely regarded as open. Partial results are known: every separable Banach space containing an isomorphic copy of c_0 can be renormed to be lush (hence to have numerical index 1), and for Asplund spaces lushness is equivalent to numerical index 1. McGregor's classical characterization handles the finite-dimensional case, and recent work (2026) has aimed at extending it to infinite dimensions, but a full intrinsic isomorphic characterization of renormability with numerical index 1 has not been established.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of Banach spaces with numerical index one
status_evidence.snippet: Although considerable progress has been made in this direction, an infinite-dimensional extension of McGregor's characterization remains elusive.
status_evidence.claim: A full characterization in the infinite-dimensional setting is still being pursued as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Numerical range of operators, numerical index of Banach spaces (lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Every separable Banach space containing an isomorphic copy of c_0 can be equivalently renormed to be lush, in particular to have numerical index 1.
status_evidence.claim: Known sufficient conditions for renorming with numerical index 1 exist, but no complete characterization.
